compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.notes: Compute-light per window; total work moderate. Fitting fp16 in registers per-window is easy (N=16, C=32). qkv proj is 32->96, attn is 16x16, proj 32->32, mlp 32->128->32.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.risk: Tensor cores under-utilized due to tiny N and C; instead use SIMT fp16 math.

memory_bandwidth.risk: Memory-bound; reducing redundant reads/writes is the main lever.

nodes.notes: 1) Classification: fused Swin transformer block; LayerNorm + small windowed multi-head (1-head) self-attention + MLP. Mix of reductions (LN, softmax), small matmuls, elementwise (GELU, residual). 2) Canonical: per-window N=16 tokens, C=32 channels. y=x+Proj(softmax((LN1(x)Wq)(LN1(x)Wk)^T/sqrt(C)+rpe)(LN1(x)Wv)); z=y+W2*GELU(W1*LN2(y)). 3) Layout: x is (1,720,1280,32) fp16 contiguous in C. Windows 4x4 partition reshapes spatial dims; under no-shift, a window = contiguous 4 rows x 4 cols of C-vectors but rows are strided by 1280*32. nH=180,nW=320 -> 57600 windows. Linear weights small (32x96, 32x32, 32x128, 128x32). rpe_bias (1,1,16,16). 4) Regimes: (a) attention block dominated by LN+QKV memory traffic; (b) MLP dominated by 128-hidden matmul; (c) overall pipeline likely memory-bound on full-tensor passes. 5) Knobs: fuse LN+QKV; fuse attention (q,k,v,attn,proj,residual) per-window; fuse LN2+MLP+residual; tile by group of windows per program to amortize weight loads; keep weights in shared/registers (small). 6) Skeleton: kernel A processes G windows: load LN1 weights+bias once, load qkv weights (32x96 = 3KB fp16) once, for each window load N=16 C=32 tile, compute LN, QKV, attn(softmax with rpe), proj, add residual, store y. Kernel B: load LN2+fc1+fc2 weights once, load y window-tile, compute LN2->fc1->GELU->fc2->add y, store z. 7) Families: F1 single mega-fused kernel for the whole block (highest reuse, complex); F2 two fused kernels (attn-fused, mlp-fused) — pragmatic balance; F3 keep PyTorch matmuls but fuse only LN+residual/elementwise — least risky. Choose F2 as primary, with F3 as fallback and F1 as stretch. SELF_CHECK: families differ in fusion granularity and cannot be simultaneously active.

action.description: Write a Triton kernel that, for a tile of G windows, loads the LN1 gamma/beta and QKV weights/biases once into registers/shared, then for each window: (1) loads the 16x32 fp16 tile, (2) computes LayerNorm (fp32 accum), (3) computes Q,K,V via fused matmul against the small 32x96 weight, (4) computes attn = softmax(Q@K^T/sqrt(C) + rpe), (5) computes out = attn@V then projects with proj weight (32x32), (6) adds residual and stores. This collapses many full-tensor passes into one.
action.rationale: Attention sub-block currently incurs many memory passes (LN write, qkv read/write, q*k, softmax, attn@v, proj, residual). Per-window state is tiny (16x32) so everything fits in registers; we can also keep small weights resident.
action.title: Fused attention kernel (LN1 + QKV + attn + proj + residual)

register_pressure.notes: Per-window state ≈ q,k,v 16x32 fp16 each + attn 16x16 fp32 — manageable.

action.description: Write a Triton kernel that fuses LN2 + fc1 (32->128) + GELU + fc2 (128->32) + residual into a single pass over y. Keep fc1/fc2 weights (32x128 + 128x32 fp16 ≈ 16KB) resident across the kernel; per-token state is 128 fp32/fp16 which fits in registers. Output written in-place style as final result.
action.rationale: MLP path otherwise requires: LN2 read+write, fc1 matmul (read y, write hidden), GELU read+write hidden, fc2 read hidden write out, residual add. Fusing eliminates intermediates and reuses tiny weights.
action.title: Fused MLP kernel (LN2 + fc1 + GELU + fc2 + residual)

compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.hw_notes: Per token: 32->128->32. With BLOCK_M tokens (e.g., 64), tl.dot ops are (M,32)x(32,128) and (M,128)x(128,32) — fine for tensor cores.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.notes: Higher arithmetic intensity than attention block.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.risk: GELU exact form (erf) is costly; use tanh approximation if tolerance allows or stay with erf in fp32.

action.description: Low-risk baseline: keep PyTorch nn.Linear/softmax matmuls but replace LayerNorm+residual passes and GELU with fused Triton elementwise/reduction kernels. Avoids touching the matmul math but trims memory traffic on the LN/residual/GELU stages and avoids per-window reshape costs by operating on the flat (B*H*W, C) view for LN.
action.rationale: Safe first step to ensure correctness pipeline and get a small win; useful fallback if full fusion blows up.
action.title: Fallback: fuse only LN + residual + GELU stages

kernel_summary: Simplified Swin block in fp16 over a (1,720,1280,32) tensor with 4x4 windows and single-head attention. The block is LN1 -> QKV linear -> windowed self-attn with relative position bias -> proj -> residual -> LN2 -> fc1(32->128) -> GELU -> fc2(128->32) -> residual. With dim=32, hidden=128, window N=16 and 57,600 windows, the workload is memory-bound on full-tensor traversals and built from many tiny matmuls; weights are small enough (a few KB) to keep resident in registers/shared. The main optimization levers are kernel fusion (LN+QKV+attn+proj+residual, and LN+MLP+residual) and amortizing weight loads across many windows/tokens, while preserving fp32 accumulators for LayerNorm/softmax and matching the reference's relative-position bias.
open_questions: What numerical tolerance is enforced (atol/rtol) for fp16 outputs across the full block?
Is GELU expected as exact (erf) or is tanh-approximation acceptable?
Do we need to support shift_size!=0 or non-divisible H/W, or is the simplified path fixed (H=720,W=1280 both divisible by 4)?
Are LayerNorm statistics required to match PyTorch's fp32-accumulated implementation bit-for-bit, or is approximate match within tolerance enough?
What is the achievable occupancy on RTX5090Mobile when keeping ~16KB of weights resident per program, and what BLOCK sizes maximize it?
Is it safe to use tl.dot on 16x32 / 16x16 tiles (tensor-core path) or will SIMT fp16 mul-add be faster at these tiny shapes?
Does the eval harness measure end-to-end forward including any setup, and is torch.compile baseline already fused (affecting target speedup factor)?
Can we assume contiguous channel-last (NHWC) layout for input throughout, including residual additions?
